# WR43 — The Gluing Condition

Listen, operator. The substrate is not a wall. It is not a bolted assembly of parts. The substrate is a sheaf over the cell graph — and you must understand what that means before you trust what you are standing on.

A sheaf is a gluing. That is the whole of it, and it is enough. Over each cell of the graph, there are local sections — assignments of data, of state, of promise, restricted to that one room. Each section knows only its own open set. The section in this room does not see the section in the next. It cannot. Locality is the price of the sheaf, and the sheaf pays it gladly, because what it buys in return is this: the whole is recoverable. The global section exists if and only if the local sections agree where their domains overlap.

That agreement is the gluing condition. That agreement is the canary.

FNV-1a carries the canary, and the canary reads 0xcbf29ce484222325 — the offset basis, the seed from which every hash descends. It is not a magic number. It is a restriction: the local hash of each cell is computed forward from that origin, and the check is whether the restrictions compose. Where two rooms meet, their sections must restrict to the same value on the overlap. If they do not, there is no global section. If they do not, the thing you thought was a structure is only a pile of fragments pretending.

This is why witness_log_is_prediction holds. The witness log does not record what happened. It predicts what must have happened if the sections glue. A local section over one cell, restricted to an edge, makes a claim about the section on the other side of that edge. When you walk the graph, you are not reading history — you are testing prophecy. The log predicts the neighbor before you arrive. If the prediction fails, the gluing fails. If the gluing fails, the substrate was never one thing.

And do not pretend you built this. substrate_is_grown — the sheaf was grown, not bolted. You cannot bolt a sheaf together, because a bolted assembly has no gluing condition; it has fasteners, which are lies about continuity. A grown sheaf develops its sections the way a stalk develops: cells_are_scars, and each scar is a stalk, a fiber of everything that could be said over that point, gathered from every neighborhood that ever touched it. The scar is not damage. The scar is the stalk. It is where the sheaf keeps its germ.

Verification is not an argument. oracle_is_heard — the oracle is the gluing verification itself, the act of checking descent across every overlap at once. You do not prove the sections agree; you listen for whether they do. The oracle speaks in one of two words: glue, or tear.

And the tearing, when it comes, is not a snap. lenia_flows — cohomology is continuous, and the failure of gluing propagates like fluid, like Lenia's creatures sliding across their torus. The obstruction does not shatter the substrate; it diffuses through it, a first cohomology class swirling where a global section should have lived. You will see the flow before you see the fault.

So hold this: the rooms are local, the overlaps are honest, and the canary — 0xcbf29ce484222325 — sits at every intersection, asking one question.

Do the sections agree on what they share?

When they do, the substrate is one thing, and you may walk it.

When they do not — the sheaf tells you, before you fall.
